vulnerabilityAlerts.description: The security label is not decoration: the dependency watchdog identifies a security pull request by this label plus Renovate authorship, and matching on the title instead produced nineteen false positives elsewhere in the fleet. Renovate's own defaults already let a vulnerability fix bypass the release-age gate and the schedule, which is why neither is restated here.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Rewrite dashboard/package-lock.json from scratch every week so transitive dependencies pick up published fixes. Ordinary updates only touch the entries named in a manifest, so an advisory against a package no manifest names is never resolved until the lockfile itself is refreshed. This is a public repository, so the run costs nothing.

packageRules.description: requires-python declares which Python versions this project supports, not which version to install, so the repository-wide rangeStrategy pin is wrong for it. Pinning turned >=3.14,<3.15 into ==3.14.7, which would make the project reject CPython 3.14.8 as incompatible the moment it ships, including a 3.14.8 published to fix a vulnerability. replace keeps the declared range and only rewrites it when a release falls outside it.
Group routine updates and merge them once Renovate observes the required checks pass. Majors are excluded so a pending major never blocks the automergeable bundle.
Majors land one at a time and are merged by a human after reading the migration notes. Public repository, so each major is proposed separately rather than bundled.
